stem: Which of the following clinical findings is most characteristic of nephritic syndrome rather than nephrotic syndrome?

options.text: Presence of red cell casts in urine

explanation: Red cell casts are a classic microscopic finding in nephritic syndrome, indicating glomerular inflammation, which is usually absent in nephrotic syndrome.
rationale: Consider which microscopic urine finding indicates active glomerular bleeding and inflammation.

optionExplanations.A: Low serum albumin is a hallmark of nephrotic syndrome due to massive protein loss, whereas it is less pronounced in pure nephritic cases.
optionExplanations.B: Nephrotic patients typically maintain normal blood pressure, while nephritic patients are frequently hypertensive due to fluid retention.
optionExplanations.C: Red cell casts are a classic microscopic finding in nephritic syndrome, indicating glomerular inflammation, which is usually absent in nephrotic syndrome.
optionExplanations.D: While both can have edema, it is the primary presenting feature and much more 'marked' in nephrotic syndrome due to low oncotic pressure.
